answer: Proof-of-Work Identity Ledger** — each identity must complete a verifiable compute task whose difficulty is set so honest agents can finish within a normal session. The ledger records every task; duplicate agents face an umber-hard replay check that rejects reused work. To enter, an attacker must fork real compute from a fresh ledge of verified history, and every extra identity adds a ripple of sequential work that cannot be parallelized for free. The per-identity cost is concrete: one full task cycle of electricity and latency, multiplied by each attempt.
